SAG-AFTRA introduces new process for hiring union actors in game pitches
SAG-AFTRA actors can now be recruited for vertical slices, demos, and other forms of content needed to pitch games.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 6, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via SAG-AFTRA
SAG-AFTRA
, the Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists, is the foremost American labor SAG-AFTRA, the Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists, has released today a new framework for using union actors in pitches and other pre-release content titled the Pre-Funding Pitch Interactive Media Agreement, specifically designed for developers creating full-featured gaming pitches. This new framework provides an opportunity for developers to use SAG-AFTRA actors in pre-production work. Previously, there were no specific union guidelines for using union actors in a pitch expected to be used to try and get a project greenlit by a publisher.
"The Pre-Funding Pitch Interactive Media Agreement streamlines the hiring of professional union talent, and that can help give devs that extra edge to get the backing they need in an extremely competitive industry," said SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director & Chief Executive Officer Duncan Crabtree-Ireland.
Related:
Zelda producer: Ocarina of Time remake helps junior staff learn classic insights
Crabtree-Ireland's comments hit on the head of how increasingly difficult it is to bring an in-development pitch to publishers and the agreement itself hits on how hiring union talent for a pitch or vertical slice is becoming more necessary.
"This agreement allows developers to up their game by bringing in professional voice and motion performance talent earlier in the process to create a higher-quality product, with the goal of capturing both imaginations and funding," said SAG-AFTRA President Sean Astin, who also played Samwise Gamgee in Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings movies.
There are a handful of rules deciding if a project is eligible for union rules, however. Any game with more than 30% of its initial production funding secured is out, as well as anything that is going to be commercially-released—which doesn't happen often, but is explicitly against the rules here.
These rules are may be an effort by the guild to ward off use of generative AI voices for pre-production use in video games. The agreement gets actors involved in the process earlier and encourages developers to avoid growing reliant on AI voices used in early development, which could lead to situations wherein AI voice acting feels like an asset
that can be iterated on without the actors
.
Ultimately, SAG-AFTRA's strategy may ensure that actors have leverage from word one, rather than feeling only tangentially involved to the project later on.
